title: COSCO Shipping Ports Q3 2026: throughput +8.4% to 42.3m TEU, overseas terminals +19.4%
summary: Q3 2026 revenue rose 13% to US$484.3m and gross profit 19.3% to US$128.1m, with attributable profit flat at US$82.6m. Total throughput reached 42.27m TEU (+8.4%); overseas terminals grew 19.4% to 11.32m TEU, driven by Piraeus (+11.4%), Chancay (+24.9%), Suez Canal Container Terminal (+8.4%), RSGT Jeddah (+19.8%) and Antwerp Gateway (+16.3%), while CSP Abu Dhabi collapsed 76.4% amid Gulf tensions. Nine-month throughput was 122.4m TEU (+8.1%). Management reiterated it will seek controlling stakes in strategic hubs and strengthen its Suez-route network, a direct overlap with DP World's core geographies.

title: COSCO Shipping Ports, China Merchants and IMC put 70% of Qingdao Dongjiakou ore terminal up for sale at CNY1.92bn
summary: COSCO Shipping Ports Investments (Shanghai) is selling its 25% stake in Qingdao Port Dongjiakou Ore Terminal alongside China Merchants Port (25%) and IMC (20%) via a public tender on the China Beijing Equity Exchange. The package carries a CNY1.92bn (US$290m) minimum price, with each 25% block floored at CNY684.9m (about US$102m). The terminal, opened in 2013 for 400,000 dwt ore carriers, posted 2025 revenue of CNY1.81bn and a CNY108m net loss. COSCO framed the exit as resource-allocation optimisation; bidding closes 11 November 2026.

title: German government moves to block COSCO's planned 80% takeover of Hamburg logistics firm Konrad Zippel
summary: Handelsblatt reported, citing an internal government memo, that Berlin intends to block COSCO's planned acquisition of 80% of Hamburg-based hinterland logistics company Konrad Zippel. The concern is that Chinese state ownership of hinterland transport serving the Port of Hamburg could become a source of political leverage, following the earlier capped 24.99% stake in HHLA's Tollerort terminal. Deal value undisclosed; the block was a reported intention rather than a final decision.

title: COSCO Shipping Ports H1 2026: record profit +28.5% to US$233.7m on 80.2m TEU
summary: First-half 2026 throughput rose 7.9% to 80.16m TEU with revenue up 12.3% to US$905.3m and attributable profit up 28.5% to US$233.7m. Overseas terminals grew 18% to 21.14m TEU, led by Chancay (+68.2% to 201,773 TEU on three mainline and five feeder services) and Wuhan (+34.6%), while Piraeus slipped 2.9% and CSP Abu Dhabi fell 44.3% on Middle East tensions. Strategy restated: controlling stakes in strategic hubs, minority stakes in gateways, port-side logistics parks and feeder networks.

title: COSCO-controlled Piraeus Port Authority creates logistics subsidiary and approves logistics expansion
summary: PPA shareholders approved statute changes on 27 August 2026 enabling a dedicated logistics subsidiary, and in October 2026 PPA approved a logistics expansion that Ports Europe reports is raising competition concerns among other port users. The move extends the COSCO-controlled operator beyond container handling into integrated logistics around Piraeus, amid EU scrutiny of Chinese port ownership and ongoing Pier I works that cut PPA H1 2026 revenue 8.9%.

title: COSCO brings in parent affiliate to fund CSP Abu Dhabi Terminal phase 2 at Khalifa Port
summary: COSCO Shipping Ports signed a subscription agreement under which COSCO (Hong Kong), a parent subsidiary, takes 40% of CSP Abu Dhabi Container Terminal for about US$14.1m, while the two shareholders extend a US$133.9m shareholder loan pro rata. The capital funds second-phase development of the terminal, described as nearing saturation, while freeing CSP capital for other projects. CSP retains 60% and operational control at Khalifa Port, competing directly with DP World's Jebel Ali.

title: Chancay marks first year of commercial operations with 502,646 TEU cumulative and feeder network to Chile, Ecuador and Panama
summary: One year after commercial start on 1 June 2025, COSCO's Chancay terminal had handled 502,646 TEU and 2.4m tonnes; Jan-May 2026 vessel calls rose 44% and tonnage 74% year on year. Services WSA3, WSA5 and ACSA1 cut Shanghai transit to 23 days, with feeders north to Panama, Guayaquil and Paita and south to four Chilean terminals. AMI analysis expects Phase 1 (1m TEU) to saturate in H2 2027, triggering a Phase 2 decision that would pull transshipment and Asia-direct cargo from DP World and APM Terminals at Callao.

title: COSCO-led consortium wins 50-year multipurpose terminal concession at Port of Tarragona
summary: The Port Authority of Tarragona awarded a consortium of COSCO Shipping Ports (51%, via Rapport Investment), COSCO Shipping Bulk and PTP Iberica (49%) a 50-year concession for a multipurpose terminal on the Andalucia Wharf, with total investment estimated at EUR144.6m (about US$156m). The 510,586 m2 site includes 58,367 m2 at the La Boella rail-port terminal and will handle containers, general cargo, vehicles and RoRo. It deepens COSCO's Spanish footprint alongside its Valencia and Bilbao terminals (3.75m TEU in 2025).

title: Chancay posts US$10.8m loss on 336,200 TEU in first full operating year 2025
summary: COSCO Shipping Ports Chancay Peru reported 2025 revenue of US$57.1m and a net loss of US$10.8m, with throughput of 336,200 TEU, roughly 14,000 short of its 350,000 TEU target, as administrative and financing costs ramped with full operations. Quarterly volumes climbed from 49,400 TEU in Q1 to 111,900 in Q3. The port helped lift Peru's 2025 exports to a record US$90bn, with exports to China up 30%.

title: COSCO Shipping Ports 2025 results: 153.0m TEU (+6.2%), revenue US$1.67bn, profit US$312m
summary: Full-year 2025 throughput rose 6.2% to 152.99m TEU with overseas terminals up 11.5% to 38.2m TEU; revenue grew 11% to US$1,669m while attributable profit edged up 1.1% to US$312.1m. Zeebrugge rose 33.1% to 894,227 TEU on new services, Piraeus fell 6% to 3.98m TEU, and Laem Chabang (consolidated from October) added 1.37m TEU. The group spent US$150.8m on equity investments and US$198.3m on berth expansion and equipment, and named Chancay, Abu Dhabi, Piraeus and Wuhan as hubs to upgrade.

title: COSCO reportedly demands majority control in BlackRock-MSC consortium for US$23bn CK Hutchison ports
summary: Per the Financial Times, COSCO demanded a majority stake in the consortium negotiating to buy CK Hutchison's 43-port, US$23bn portfolio, after initially being expected to take a minority share; BlackRock and MSC/TiL reportedly would not accept, leaving talks at an impasse. Beijing had pressed for COSCO's inclusion since mid-2025. By August 2026 CK Hutchison said there was nothing to report on the transaction, with Panama concessions cancelled and under arbitration. The outcome would reshape the global terminal league table against DP World.

title: COSCO Shipping Ports injects US$20.6m into US JV to wind up SSA Terminals (Seattle) stake
summary: COSCO Shipping Ports and partner China Shipping North Control injected US$20.57m into COSCO Shipping Terminals (USA) LLC (40%/60%) to meet obligations from the liquidation of SSA Terminals (Seattle), in which the JV held one third. The Seattle terminal suspended operations in 2025 after new stormwater discharge rules, with throughput dropping to zero from 143,447 TEU in 2024. The exit removes a non-core US associate and limits contingent liabilities amid a hostile US environment for Chinese port investors.

title: COSCO Shipping Ports among operators at Panama Canal's call for Atlantic and Pacific terminal partners
summary: The Panama Canal Authority launched a process to identify partners to develop new container terminals on both coasts, with COSCO Shipping Ports, CMA Terminals, DP World, APM Terminals, PSA, TiL, SSA Marine and others attending the first meeting. The process moves through a feasibility study and project plan to a concessionaire selection expected to conclude in Q4 2026. It is a potential new Latin American hub battleground given COSCO's Chancay build-out and the stalled CK Hutchison Panama assets.

title: COSCO Shipping Ports completes US$110m purchase of stakes in Hutchison's Laem Chabang terminals
summary: COSCO Shipping Ports closed its acquisition of 12.5% of Thai Laemchabang Terminal (Berth A2) and 30% of Hutchison Laemchabang Terminal (Berths A3, C1-C2, D1-D3, under construction) for about US$110m, first announced in October 2024. The berths will offer around 6.7m TEU annual capacity at Thailand's largest deep-water port, which handles about 80% of the country's boxes. TLT has been consolidated since October 2025 and contributed 1.37m TEU in 2025, anchoring COSCO in the Eastern Economic Corridor.

title: COSCO Shipping Ports pivots M&A hunt to Southeast Asia, South America, Africa and Middle East amid trade war
summary: At its interim results briefing, managing director Wu Yu said international investment faced challenges from a volatile geopolitical environment, tightening foreign-investment screening and high bid prices from rival operators. With China's exports shifting to emerging markets, the company said it is seeking acquisitions in Southeast Asia, South America, Africa and the Middle East, the same frontier geographies DP World prioritises. Wu declined to comment on COSCO's possible role in the CK Hutchison sale.

title: Beijing threatens to block CK Hutchison ports sale unless COSCO gets a stake
summary: The Wall Street Journal reported Chinese officials told the parties the US$22.8bn sale of CK Hutchison's 43-terminal portfolio to BlackRock and MSC would be blocked if COSCO were left out. CK Hutchison later confirmed in a 28 July filing that it had invited a major Chinese strategic investor, identified by sources as COSCO, to join the consortium after exclusivity with BlackRock-MSC lapsed; reports suggested COSCO could take a stake in 41 ports excluding the two Panama terminals.

title: Brazil and China discuss bi-oceanic railway linking COSCO's Chancay port to Brazilian interior
summary: Brazil's Planning Minister Simone Tebet said Brazil was in talks with China's state railway group on a rail link from Chancay to Brazil, favouring a southern route via Acre and Tocantins to Bahia connecting to the FIOL railway rather than an Amazon alignment. She estimated five to eight years to build. The corridor would feed Brazilian cargo to COSCO's US$1.3bn Pacific hub, shortening routes to China by at least 10,000 km and bypassing Atlantic ports.

title: COSCO launches monthly PCTC service to Piraeus car terminal with Geely vehicles
summary: The COSCO Shipping Car Carriers vessel COSCO Sheng Shi (5,276 CEU) made its maiden Piraeus call, discharging 199 Geely cars and 17 electric buses and inaugurating a regular monthly service. PPA said the call cements Piraeus as an Eastern Mediterranean vehicle transshipment hub and announced plans to expand the car terminal through infrastructure, automation and green investments, part of COSCO's wider EUR610m approved Piraeus investment plan.

title: Xi Jinping inaugurates COSCO's US$1.3bn Chancay megaport, China's largest South American port investment
summary: Presidents Xi Jinping and Dina Boluarte inaugurated the COSCO-controlled (60%) Chancay terminal, 78 km north of Lima, with Phase 1 investment of about US$1.3bn rising to US$3.4bn at full build-out of 15 berths. The initial 1,500 m of quay with 17.8 m draught handles 24,000 TEU ships, with design capacity of 1m TEU, 6m tonnes of bulk and 160,000 vehicles a year and direct Shanghai services of 23 days. It is COSCO's first greenfield hub in South America and a direct challenge to DP World and APM Terminals at Callao.

title: COSCO Shipping Ports plans US$375m investment in Egyptian ports including Ain Sokhna
summary: COSCO Shipping Ports Chief Accountant Zhao Fengnian told Asharq Business the company would invest US$375m in Egyptian ports during 2024 to expand container capacity, including at Ain Sokhna where COSCO holds 25% of the new Hutchison-led Sokhna container terminal and participates in Suez Canal Container Terminal at Port Said. The plan places COSCO head-to-head with DP World Sokhna, which announced an US$80m logistics park the same month.

title: China Merchants Port withdraws from US$392m South Asia Commercial and Logistics Hub at Port of Colombo
summary: China Merchants Port disclosed in an HKEX filing that the 50-year BOT joint venture for the South Asia Commercial and Logistics Hub in Colombo (CMPort 70% via Fortune Centre Group, SLPA 15%, Access Engineering 15%) would not proceed, citing changes in the project timetable and implementation environment. SLPA put the investment at about US$280m for 150,000 m2 of bonded warehousing and CFS; roughly US$29.8m is being refunded to shareholders. The project had stalled after Sri Lanka withdrew strategic-development tax concessions under IMF commitments; SLPA will re-tender under a PPP model.

title: China Merchants Port offers its 25% of Qingdao Dongjiakou Ore Terminal in CNY1.92bn joint sale with COSCO and IMC
summary: China Merchants Port, through Mighty Star Investment, is selling its 25% stake in Qingdao Port Dongjiakou Ore Terminal in a single 70% package with COSCO Shipping Ports (25%) and IMC (20%) via the China Beijing Equity Exchange, with a CNY684.9m (about US$102m) floor on its block. The loss-making iron-ore terminal (2025 net loss CNY108m) is a non-core bulk asset; CMPort said the sale realises the investment's value and improves financial flexibility. Initial disclosure period runs to 11 November 2026.

title: China Merchants Port ranked world's second-largest terminal operator by DynaLiners with 66.0m TEU handled in 2025
summary: DynaLiners' 2025 terminal-operator ranking placed China Merchants Port second with 66.0m TEU handled (+8% from 61.2m), ahead of COSCO Shipping Ports at fourth (58.2m TEU, +7%) and CMA CGM/Terminal Link eighth (15.8m TEU, +22%). The ranking underlines CMPort's scale, built mostly on its West Shenzhen stronghold and Chinese hub stakes, versus DP World's more geographically diversified network.

title: China Merchants Port 2025 results: throughput 151.3m TEU (+3.8%) but profit down 18.5% to HK$6.46bn
summary: China Merchants Port Holdings reported 2025 attributable profit of HK$6.46bn (about US$828m), down 18.5%, despite revenue rising 12.8% to HK$13.35bn, blaming a HK$1.45bn fall in associates' contribution and HK$605m higher credit-loss provisions. Group container throughput rose 3.8% to 151.29m TEU, with terminals outside Greater China up 5.7% to 38.94m TEU (Brazil TCP, Togo Lome, Turkey Kumport cited); bulk volumes fell 5.3% to 530m tonnes. Net gearing was 19.3% and the final dividend was cut to HK$0.489.

title: China seeks deeper shipping and port cooperation with Malta, where China Merchants Port holds Malta Freeport stake
summary: After a Beijing meeting with Maltese representatives, China's Commerce Ministry said it wants to deepen cooperation in shipping and port logistics with Malta. Reuters noted China Merchants Port already holds a stake in Malta Freeport Terminals (via Terminal Link, its JV with CMA CGM), a major Mediterranean transshipment hub, as part of Belt and Road investment. No new transaction was announced, but it signals state backing for CMPort's Mediterranean position.

title: China Merchants and COSCO tipped as bidders for PSA's 20% stake in Hutchison Ports (~US$4bn)
summary: Bloomberg reported that China Merchants Port and COSCO Shipping Ports had both expressed interest in PSA International's 20% stake in Hutchison Ports, which PSA is reportedly seeking to sell for about US$4bn after holding it since 2006. The interest emerged as CK Hutchison's 80% was under sale to a BlackRock-MSC consortium opposed by Beijing. A Chinese state buyer for the PSA block would keep a Chinese foothold across Hutchison's 43-port network.

title: CMA Terminals completes purchase of 49% of Nador West Med container terminal from Marsa Maroc
summary: Marsa Maroc announced regulatory clearance and completion of CMA Terminals' acquisition of 49% of Nador Container Terminal, concessionaire of the West Terminal at Nador West Med, with Marsa Maroc keeping 51%. The terminal offers 900 m of quay, 18 m draught, 37.5 ha of yard and 60 ha total, eight STS cranes and ultimate capacity of 1.8m TEU, with operations due from 2027 as the US$5.6bn port opens. It gives CMA CGM a Western Mediterranean transshipment hub adjacent to Tanger Med, where it already operates with Eurogate.

title: Latakia International Container Terminal takes delivery of six Konecranes hybrid RTGs under CMA CGM's EUR230m plan
summary: CMA Terminals' Latakia International Container Terminal, operated since 2009 and now under a 30-year concession signed in May 2025, received six Konecranes hybrid RTGs worth over EUR16m. The delivery is part of an announced EUR230m programme including up to EUR200m for a new berth over four years, in which AD Ports Group agreed in November 2025 to take 20% for AED81m. CMA CGM is positioning Latakia as Syria's main gateway as DP World rebuilds Tartous under its US$800m deal.

title: CMA CGM launches EUR92m Beirut container terminal expansion to lift capacity from 1.2m to 2.8m TEU
summary: CMA CGM and port authority GEPB launched a EUR92m (about US$100m) expansion of the Beirut container terminal, operated by CMA Terminals under a 10-year concession since March 2022. Over roughly 18 months the yard grows from 45 to 80 ha, with a new feeder quay and two mobile cranes, a customs scanner area, automated gates, a heavy-haul bridge and hybrid equipment, raising capacity from 1.2m to 2.8m TEU. A groundbreaking on Berth 16 in early October 2026 was attended by PM Nawaf Salam and the Saudi ambassador, three months after Riyadh lifted its export ban on Lebanon.
partners: Gestion et Exploitation du Port de Beyrouth (GEPB)

title: CMA CGM signs MoU with China Communications Construction Company on ports, logistics and energy transition
summary: CMA CGM and state-owned CCCC signed a memorandum of understanding in Marseille covering cooperation on port infrastructure, logistics and energy-transition projects across Africa, Southeast Asia, the Middle East, Latin America and China. Pairing the world's third-largest carrier's terminal arm with China's biggest port EPC contractor creates a build-and-operate combination that could compete for greenfield concessions in DP World's African and Middle Eastern markets.

title: RSGT and CMA CGM finalise SAR1.6bn (US$434m) agreement for Jeddah Islamic Port Terminal 4
summary: Red Sea Gateway Terminal and CMA CGM signed the definitive agreement to jointly develop and operate the new Terminal 4 at Jeddah Islamic Port, an investment of about SAR1.6bn (US$434m) in collaboration with Mawani, formalising the October 2025 agreement (then quoted at SAR1.7bn). The JV, owned by RSGT and CMA Terminals, gives CMA CGM a dedicated Red Sea hub alongside its RSGT shareholding and comes amid rerouting pressures from the US-Iran conflict; it competes with DP World's Jeddah South Container Terminal.

title: CMA CGM and Stonepeak close United Ports LLC: Stonepeak invests US$2.4bn for 25% of CMA CGM's US terminal portfolio
summary: CMA CGM and infrastructure investor Stonepeak completed formation of United Ports LLC after regulatory approvals, a US-based joint venture holding CMA CGM's equity interests in nine container terminals across five countries (reported as 10 ports in the January 2026 announcement), valued at about US$10bn. Stonepeak invested US$2.4bn for 25%, with CMA CGM retaining control. The vehicle supports CMA CGM's US$20bn US investment pledge and recapitalises its terminal arm for further acquisitions.

title: CMA CGM launches weekly Iberimar short-sea loop linking Algeciras, Vigo, Valencia, Castellon, Las Palmas, Tanger Med and Casablanca
summary: CMA CGM merged its Agapome and Mosth1 shuttles into a single weekly Iberimar service covering seven ports across Spain, Portugal and Morocco, including Algeciras, Vigo, Valencia, Castellon, Las Palmas, Tanger Med and Casablanca. The consolidated loop feeds its Tanger Med and future Nador hubs and strengthens Iberia-Morocco short-sea coverage, a corridor also served by DP World's Unifeeder.

title: Syria awards CMA CGM operation of dry ports in Adra and Aleppo free zones, with rail revival to Latakia
summary: Syria's General Authority for Ports and Customs signed an agreement for CMA CGM to operate two dry ports inside the Adra (Damascus) and Aleppo free zones, aimed at restarting freight rail links suspended for 14 years and connecting them to CMA Terminals' Latakia gateway. In July 2026 CMA CGM added a Damascus air-cargo and dry-ports deal. The hinterland network builds an integrated Syrian corridor competing with DP World's Tartous redevelopment.
partners: Syrian General Authority for Ports and Customs

title: Luka Rijeka opens due diligence as CMA CGM emerges as potential buyer of controlling stake
summary: Luka Rijeka d.d., the main dry-cargo concessionaire at Croatia's Port of Rijeka, approved a due-diligence process at the request of largest shareholder Port Acquisitions a.s., which is considering selling its stake to CMA CGM. CMA CGM already calls Rijeka with its Bora Med service and deployed the 2025 record-size CMA CGM Adonis there. A deal would give the group an Adriatic gateway to Central Europe alongside its Koper and Trieste intermodal links.

title: CMA CGM acquires Lebanon's Fattal Group to extend logistics footprint behind Beirut terminal
summary: CMA CGM Chairman Rodolphe Saade announced the acquisition of Lebanon-based Fattal Group, expanding the group's logistics and distribution business in Lebanon alongside its Beirut container terminal concession. Saade said the group remains committed to investing in Lebanon despite regional instability. Terms were not disclosed. The deal integrates terminal, logistics and distribution in a market where DP World has no port presence.

title: CMA Terminals Khalifa Port to expand capacity 50% to 2.7m TEU in AED420m deal with AD Ports
summary: AD Ports Group and CMA CGM agreed an AED420m (US$115m) expansion of CMA Terminals Khalifa Port (CMA CGM 70%, AD Ports 30%) less than a year after its December 2024 opening, as the terminal reached full capacity. Quay grows from 800 m to 1,200 m and yard from 464,000 m2 to 667,000 m2, raising capacity from 1.8m to 2.7m TEU and Khalifa Port's total to 10.5m TEU, with completion in early 2028. The rail-linked terminal competes directly with DP World's Jebel Ali for UAE gateway and transshipment cargo.

title: CMA CGM to take 20% of Eurogate Container Terminal Hamburg and co-finance Westerweiterung
summary: CMA CGM and Eurogate announced a strategic partnership under which CMA CGM takes a 20% stake in Eurogate Container Terminal Hamburg and co-finances the planned Westerweiterung (western expansion) of the terminal. The framework agreement extends the two groups' existing cooperation at Tanger Med and Wilhelmshaven and secures CMA CGM dedicated capacity at Germany's largest port, where COSCO holds 24.99% of HHLA's Tollerort and MSC co-owns HHLA.

title: AD Ports Group takes 20% of CMA CGM's Latakia International Container Terminal for AED81m
summary: AD Ports Group agreed to acquire 20% of Latakia International Container Terminal (LICT), Syria's main container gateway operated by CMA Terminals, for AED81m (US$22m), and to invest jointly with CMA CGM in the terminal's EUR230m expansion including a new berth. The partnership pairs CMA CGM's 30-year concession with Gulf capital, mirroring the two groups' JVs at Khalifa Port and Pointe-Noire, and sets up a Latakia-versus-Tartous (DP World) rivalry on the Syrian coast.

title: CMA CGM opens Sfax-Tanger Med-Valencia short-sea service timed to Tunisian date exports
summary: CMA CGM launched a new short-sea route linking Sfax in Tunisia with its Tanger Med hub in Morocco and Valencia in Spain, timed to the start of the Tunisian date export season. The service adds a Maghreb feeder leg into the group's Western Mediterranean hub system and strengthens its reefer and agrifood short-sea offering, a segment also targeted by DP World's Unifeeder in the Mediterranean.

title: CMA CGM acquires UK rail freight operator Freightliner
summary: CMA CGM announced the acquisition of Freightliner's UK rail and road intermodal operations, inland terminals, port connections and brand, excluding the Heavy Haul business, with closing expected in early 2026 pending approvals. Freightliner is the UK's largest maritime intermodal rail operator, giving CMA CGM control of hinterland flows from Southampton, Felixstowe and London Gateway (DP World's UK hub). Terms were not disclosed.

title: CMA CGM accelerates EUR200m second phase of Latakia port expansion after Damascus talks
summary: Following a Damascus meeting between CEO Rodolphe Saade and Syria's leadership, CMA CGM said it would accelerate the EUR200m second phase of the Latakia port expansion under its 30-year concession, bringing total committed investment to about EUR230m. The programme includes a new deep-water berth over four years and new handling equipment, and anticipates the Adra/Aleppo dry-port and rail deals that followed in 2026.

title: CMA CGM signals interest in joining a new solution for CK Hutchison's global ports sale
summary: CMA CGM confirmed it was closely following the proposed sale of CK Hutchison's port operations and was open to joining a new solution after exclusive talks between CK Hutchison and the BlackRock-MSC consortium expired. The statement positioned CMA Terminals/Terminal Link as a potential alternative or co-investor to COSCO in the US$23bn, 43-port transaction, which remained stalled as of August 2026.

title: CMA CGM signs 30-year concession to develop and operate Syria's Latakia port
summary: Syria signed a 30-year contract with CMA CGM to develop and run the Mediterranean port of Latakia, announced by regional director Joseph Dakak at the presidential palace in Damascus in the presence of interim President Ahmed al-Sharaa. It converts CMA Terminals' operating contract (held since 2009 and renewed in February 2025) into a long-term concession and was followed by a EUR230m investment programme. It pre-dated DP World's US$800m Tartous agreement by two weeks, setting up a two-operator Syrian coast.

title: CMA CGM takes 35% stake and management contract in Egypt's October Dry Port
summary: During President Macron's state visit to Cairo, CMA CGM signed for a 35% stake in October Dry Port (ODP), Egypt's first inland dry port west of Cairo, together with a management contract. The deal supports development of Egypt's rail-connected logistics platform linking Alexandria and Sokhna gateways to the 6th of October industrial zone, and complements CMA Terminals' Tahya Misr terminal in Alexandria. It competes with DP World's Sokhna-Cairo logistics corridor.

title: CMA CGM pledges US$20bn investment in US maritime sector over four years
summary: CEO Rodolphe Saade announced at the White House a US$20bn (EUR18.5bn) four-year investment programme to revitalise the American maritime sector, spanning port terminal capacity, logistics, US-flagged vessels and air cargo. The pledge underpinned the subsequent United Ports LLC joint venture with Stonepeak, which pooled CMA CGM's US terminal interests with US$2.4bn of outside capital.

title: AD Ports and CMA Terminals form JV to develop and operate New East Mole multipurpose terminal at Pointe-Noire
summary: AD Ports Group and CMA CGM, through CMA Terminals, agreed to jointly develop, manage and operate the New East Mole multipurpose terminal at Pointe-Noire, Republic of Congo, where CMA Terminals already runs the Congo Terminal container facility. The JV extends the two groups' partnership from Khalifa Port into Central Africa and adds a Gulf-backed competitor on the Gulf of Guinea coast where DP World operates in Angola, Senegal and Nigeria.

title: CMA CGM launches weekly IAX1 feeder linking Izmit and Ambarli with Varna and Burgas
summary: CMA CGM introduced the IAX1, a weekly feeder service with a 700 TEU vessel connecting Izmit and Ambarli in Turkey with the Bulgarian ports of Varna and Burgas from 22 January 2025. The dedicated Black Sea loop improves Bulgarian connectivity to CMA CGM's Turkish hubs and competes with regional feeder operators including DP World's Unifeeder in the Black Sea.

title: Eurofos (CMA CGM/Terminal Link) renews Fos-sur-Mer Terminal de Mediterranee concession to 2046
summary: Eurofos, the CMA CGM-controlled operator of the Terminal de Mediterranee at Fos-sur-Mer, renewed its concession with the Port of Marseille Fos to 2046, covering berths 862-864 in Dock 2 with 750 m of quay and 33.9 ha of land. The renewal secures CMA CGM's home-port hub, which received new cranes in November 2024, and was announced alongside the group's 30-year inland Port of Lyon sub-concession on the Rhone.

title: CMA CGM-led consortium wins 30-year sub-concession for inland Port of Lyon
summary: A consortium led by CMA CGM with Banque des Territoires and the regional Chambers of Commerce and Industry won a 30-year sub-concession for the inland Port of Lyon (Edouard Herriot), aiming to double containerised cargo moving on the Rhone from Marseille Fos. The award vertically integrates CMA CGM's Fos terminals with river barging and inland logistics in France's second city.

title: CMA CGM launches six-vessel Bora Med short-sea service linking Adriatic and Eastern Mediterranean
summary: CMA CGM's Short Sea Lines division launched the weekly Bora Med Service (BMS) with six vessels from Antalya on 23 December 2024, linking Adriatic ports (Koper, Trieste, Venice, Ravenna, Ancona, Rijeka, Bar) with the Eastern Mediterranean (Antalya, Izmir, Gemlik, Ambarli, Limassol, Beirut, Alexandria, Marsaxlokk). The service was revised in February 2025 to add Syrian ports and Rijeka, reinforcing CMA CGM's intra-Med feeder network as Red Sea diversions reshaped Mediterranean flows.

title: CMA CGM and Marsa Maroc sign 25-year, US$280m Nador West Med container terminal concession
summary: CMA CGM and Marsa Maroc agreed to form a joint venture for a 25-year concession covering 750 m of quay and 35 ha of yard, half of the Nador West Med container terminal, with US$280m investment and 1.2m TEU annual capacity, expanding STS cranes from six to eight and electric RTGs from 15 to 24 for 18 m-draught megamax ships. Marsa Maroc holds 51% and CMA Terminals 49% (completed October 2026). It positions CMA CGM at Morocco's second deep-water hub after Tanger Med, where DP World has no presence.
